content.title: About
content.content: Potato French Fries NFS (4216) are thin strips of potato that are deep‑fried until golden and crisp. The product is made from selected varieties of potatoes that are blanched, dried and lightly coated with vegetable oil before frying. The fries have a crunchy exterior and a soft, aromatic interior.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: The term “fries” comes from the English word “fried”.
French fries first appeared in the United States in the early 1920s as a street snack.
There are more than 30 cutting styles for fries: classic, steak, curly, waffle, etc.
In 2015 NFS launched a production line that can produce fries with less than 10 % fat.
Fries are commonly served with sauces such as ketchup, mayonnaise, cheese sauce, and barbecue.

items.title: Source of potassium
items.content: Potatoes are rich in potassium, which supports normal heart and muscle function.

items.title: Vitamin C
items.content: Fresh potatoes contain vitamin C, an antioxidant that helps protect cells.

items.title: Dietary fiber
items.content: Fiber in potatoes aids digestion and promotes a feeling of fullness.

items.title: Complex carbohydrates
items.content: French fries provide complex carbs that serve as an energy source.

items.title: Beta‑carotene
items.content: Yellow and orange potatoes contain beta‑carotene, which the body converts to vitamin A.

items.title: High fat content
items.content: Deep‑frying adds a significant amount of fat, increasing the calorie density.

items.title: Salt
items.content: Fries are often salted; excessive sodium intake can affect blood pressure.

items.title: Acrylamide
items.content: Cooking at very high temperatures can form acrylamide, a potentially harmful compound.

items.title: Potato allergy
items.content: Rarely, some individuals may experience an allergic reaction to potatoes.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Serve hot as a side dish or a snack. Sprinkle with salt, spices, cheese powder, or dip in various sauces. For a healthier option, bake or air‑fry the fries instead of deep‑frying.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Keep frozen fries in an airtight bag at –18 °C. Once thawed, cook immediately to preserve quality. Cooked fries should be consumed within 2 hours at room temperature.
